# Arrow keys right after a button menu opens have no witness

## Context

#6033 (open since 2024-10) reports that after opening the menu in `examples/button/base`, arrow keys no longer navigate right away, and suspects a missing `focus()` call. It is fixed on `dev`. A real-Chromium probe of that example at `5d375d9722`:

| opened by | focus right after opening | ArrowDown | ArrowDown |
|---|---|---|---|
| click | `Item 1` (`LI` in `.neo-menu-list`) | `Item 2` | `Item 3` (a parent; its submenu previews) |
| Enter on the focused button | `Item 1` | `Item 2` | `Item 3` |
| Space on the focused button | `Item 1` | `Item 2` | `Item 3` |
| CONTROL: no menu opened | `BODY`, no menu | nothing moves | |

No committed test asserts it, so #6033 cannot close on evidence that stays true.

## The Problem

What makes it work today is one line far from the button: `component.Base#afterSetMounted` focuses a floating component when it mounts, unless `focusOnMount` is false. #18765 added that flag so a hover preview does not steal focus. A later change that narrows the default or the floating branch would break #6033 again, and nothing would notice. The closest arm, `component/menu/SpawnAnimation.spec.mjs` › *arrow-key navigation works during the entrance window*, focuses the first item itself before pressing a key, so it passes whether or not opening the menu hands focus over.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/button/Base.mjs#toggleMenu()` shows the floating `menuList` created with `parentComponent: me`.
- `src/component/Base.mjs:775` runs `me.focusOnMount && me.focus(me.id, true)` for a floating component on mount, and focus lands on the first item.
- The `Navigator` moves the active item on ArrowDown once focus is inside the list.
- `test/playwright/component/button/Base.spec.mjs` has no menu arm.

## The Fix

Arms in `test/playwright/component/button/Base.spec.mjs`, on a Button with a three-item `menu` created in the component harness. Open the menu by click, by Enter and by Space on the focused button, then press ArrowDown without any explicit focus call. Assert that focus moved from the first item to the second.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — the arms pass for click, Enter and Space on `dev`.
- [ ] **AC-2** — they fail when the opened menu does not take focus on mount (mutation receipt in the PR), so they witness the hand-off rather than the Navigator.
- [ ] **AC-3** — #6033 carries the probe receipt and a pointer to the arms (post-merge: closed as completed).

## Out of Scope

- Any change to focus, menu or Navigator behaviour.
